topic: Preventing duplicate POST creation with idempotency keys
tomorrowTopic: Testing concurrent idempotent POST retries with Testcontainers

hook.headline: A timeout can hide a successful POST
hook.hook: If the client retries after losing the response, the server may receive the same creation intent twice. Make that intent identifiable.
hook.visualCaption: Same client intent plus same key should resolve to one committed business outcome.
hook.microExample: POST times out → retry same key → return original outcome

mentalModel.title: Deduplicate intent, not transport
mentalModel.coreIdea: POST is not idempotent by HTTP method semantics. An API can add application-level idempotency by binding a client-supplied key to one request intent and storing the resulting outcome durably.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Retries become safe only when duplicate requests converge on the same durable business result.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: same intent + same key → same outcome

code.title: Make duplicate keys impossible
code.intro: Persist the key with tenant or client scope and let PostgreSQL enforce uniqueness under concurrency.
code.code:
CREATE TABLE idempotency_record (
  client_id bigint NOT NULL,
  idem_key text NOT NULL,
  request_hash text NOT NULL,
  response_body jsonb,
  PRIMARY KEY (client_id, idem_key)
);
code.highlightReason: The composite primary key makes concurrent claims for the same client and idempotency key mutually exclusive at the database constraint level.
code.takeaway: A pre-check such as SELECT then INSERT is not sufficient by itself because two requests can both observe absence before either inserts.
code.professionalNote: Store enough request identity to reject accidental key reuse with different payload semantics, and define retention and response-replay rules explicitly.

production.title: Design the whole retry path
production.scenario: A checkout POST commits an order, but the connection drops before the client receives the 201 response. The client retries automatically with the same application-level idempotency key.
problems: Without deduplication, both requests can create separate orders even though the user intended one purchase.
A cache-only key can disappear or diverge from the committed database state unless its consistency model is deliberately designed.
production.professionalApproach: Scope the key, enforce uniqueness in durable storage, bind it to the request intent, and coordinate the idempotency record with the business write so a committed outcome can be replayed. Treat retries with the same key but different intent as a conflict rather than silently accepting them.
production.debugClue: Two resources share the same client operation context, while request logs show a timeout followed by a retry of the same creation call.

interview.question: A client times out after POST /orders and retries. How would you prevent duplicate orders?
interview.answer: I would not assume POST is idempotent. I would require an application-level idempotency key for retryable creation requests, scope it to the caller, persist it with a database uniqueness constraint, and associate it with the request intent and committed result. A retry with the same key can then return the stored outcome; the same key with materially different input should be rejected. The database constraint matters because a check-then-insert sequence alone races under concurrent requests.
remember: Same key must represent the same intent
